topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maria Chen (VerdantTech Procurement), Ethan Blake (VerdantTech Legal), Priya Nair (VerdantTech Head of Platform), Jason Lee (VerdantTech CTO)

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we really appreciate it. Quick intro, I'm Samantha Park, AE on the account, with Diego our SE.
[00:12] Diego: hi all, Diego here - i'll be your technical lead for the procurement and onboarding stuff.
[00:18] Maria: Hi Maria here, procurement. We wanted to run through the MSA/DPA timing, SLA language, and understand the pricing for Dedicated and Private.
[00:27] Ethan: Ethan from legal - we'll be handling the DPA redlines and any SLA exposure.
[00:31] Priya: Priya, platform lead. We'll own the technical validation and benchmark requirements.
[00:36] Jason: Jason, CTO. We're keeping an eye on latency and data residency.

[00:45] Samantha: Great. Agenda - quick overview of the docs we already shared, confirm what you're after on SLAs and residency, pricing tiers, and next steps. We'll also capture any competitor concerns.

[01:05] Diego: Quick note - the spreadsheet we shared has Dedicated and Private price buckets, and an optional SLA uplift for 99.9 vs 99.95 availability. The technical deep dive will show typical p95/p99 latencies on our hosted and dedicated stacks.

[01:28] Maria: Timeline wise procurement wants a doc stack we can share with finance by next week. So if you can get us the MSA + DPA drafts and pricing that'd be ideal.

[01:40] Samantha: Absolutely - we'll send the MSA and DPA today as drafts, and the pricing sheet with line items for pilot and committed capacity.

[02:05] Ethan: On the DPA, a few flag items from our side: data residency, subprocessors list, and encryption at rest - we use a KMS and will need to see key management integration options. Also, retention periods and deletion certification language.

[02:22] Diego: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; for Hosted we provide BYOK options with rotation support. Note: the on-prem package requires some network allowance and install windows.

[02:45] Priya: Can you clarify the difference in guarantees between Dedicated and Private? We may need stricter SLAs and regional isolation.

[02:58] Samantha: Short answer: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and SLA-backed throughput guarantees; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full network isolation and can include custom SLA terms. Pricing moves up for Private due to operational overhead and support.

[03:20] Jason: In terms of security certifications - do you have SOC 2 Type II and pen test reports? Our security team will request those.

[03:31] Diego: Yes, SOC 2 Type II report is available; we also have a security whitepaper and recent pen test summary. We'll share the artifacts and if needed, a secure link to the full report.

[03:50] Ethan: Great. Also need to know about audit logs and retention - we log per-request metadata and support export to SIEM. Is that available in Hosted? In Dedicated?

[04:08] Diego: Audit logs are available across all modes. Hosted has log export integrations (e.g., forward to customer SIEM via VPC peering), Dedicated includes more controls and longer retention as part of the package, Private can be configured to send logs to customer-managed endpoints.

[04:30] Maria: Procurement question: what triggers the enterprise pricing? We have a pilot for Q3 but procurement needs to know thresholds for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go.

[04:45] Samantha: We typically move to committed monthly/annual contracts for Dedicated once usage is steady - the pricing sheet will show breakpoints: pilot (small commitment), reserved pools for sustained throughput, and enterprise contracts with volume discounts.

[05:10] Priya: On the technical side, Diego - we want to run a benchmark comparing latency at typical prompt lengths and KV cache behavior; can you describe the expected perf and what you need from us?

[05:25] Diego: We'll need a representative prompt set and traffic profile (QPS, tokens per request). For Dedicated we'll run sustained load tests and collect p95/p99, for Hosted we can run spike tests. Also we'll measure cold-start behavior and KV cache hit rates.

[05:50] Jason: Data residency - we need EU-only hosting for certain customer data. Does Redwood support region pinning for hosted infra or do we need Private?

[06:01] Samantha: We have region pinning in Hosted for certain models/regions but for strict EU-only residency Private or Dedicated in specific cloud regions is the safer route. We'll capture specifics in the DPA.

[06:18] Ethan: On indemnity and liability - we need to understand the SLA credit mechanics and liability cap. Our legal typically asks for a multiple-of-fees cap.

[06:34] Samantha: Standard SLA credits are service-credit based and liability caps are in the MSA; we can review and flag items for negotiation.

[06:50] Maria: Procurement also needs the PO process and lead times for onboarding once MSA is signed. What's typical?

[07:02] Diego: Once contracts are signed and payment set, pilot onboarding is usually 2-3 weeks for hosted; Dedicated provisioning can take 4-8 weeks depending on capacity and region; Private on-prem scheduling varies (4-12 weeks) depending on site readiness.

[07:25] Samantha: We'll include a timeline in the email - and a checklist of documents and IT contacts we need.

[07:40] Priya: About backups and data separation - can you confirm that customer data in Dedicated is logically separated and how backups are handled?

[07:55] Diego: Dedicated provides tenant isolation on the serving layer and storage. Backups are per-customer and we can agree retention windows. For highly regulated workloads we recommend Private with customer-owned keying.

[08:15] Ethan: A quick question on access controls - SSO/SAML and RBAC support? We need SSO and audit trail of admin actions.

[08:28] Diego: Yes SSO (SAML/OAuth) and fine-grained RBAC are supported in the Console; audit trail for admin actions is included in the enterprise package.

[08:45] Maria: Any vendor references from similar size customers you can share? We want to validate operations.

[08:54] Samantha: We can share anonymized references and a short case study for a health-care customer with similar residency needs - will attach.

[09:05] Jason: On pricing for the SLA uplift - what's the delta from 99.9 to 99.95? I know it's small in absolute terms for big infra but procurement needs the number.

[09:18] Samantha: The uplift varies by capacity but typically 8-15% on top of base Dedicated pricing; we'll put exact numbers in the pricing sheet for your expected commit level.

[09:35] Priya: Do you offer a trial credit for the pilot to run the bench? That helps us reduce procurement friction.

[09:42] Samantha: Yes, we usually offer pilot credits and a timeboxed evaluation - we'll include that in the pricing proposal.

[09:55] Ethan: About subprocessors - please include the current list and a process for adding new ones; we need notice periods in the DPA.

[10:07] Diego: We'll include current subprocessors and the standard 30-day notice for additions; if needed we can negotiate tighter terms.

[10:20] Maria: Ok - next steps from procurement view: need MSA + DPA drafts, pricing with pilot credit + SLA uplift numbers, and SOC2 and pen test artifacts.

[10:32] Samantha: We'll deliver those. Diego will set up the technical deep dive and benchmark.

[10:40] Jason: One more technical ask - for the benchmark we may want to test quantized model variants for throughput/cost tradeoff, are those supported?

[10:52] Diego: Yes, we support different quantization profiles and can show cost/latency tradeoffs per model variant. We'll need sample prompts and expected response lengths.

[11:10] Ethan: Legal question - would Redwood entertain custom SLA language for a full enterprise contract? We may want different remedies.

[11:22] Samantha: We can discuss custom SLA language at enterprise deal stage; standard terms are in the MSA but high-commit customers often negotiate tailored SLAs.

[11:35] Maria: Procurement timeline: If we get drafts by Friday and legal turns DPA redlines by next Wednesday, we could sign in late July. Is that consistent with your timelines?

[11:48] Samantha: Yes that's doable. We'll target sending docs today/Friday and expect redlines mid-next week.

[12:05] Priya: Any blockers we should be aware of? From our infra side we need a staging VPC and some IP allowlist windows for the tests.

[12:17] Diego: Noted - we'll include network requirements in the onboarding checklist.

[12:30] Jason: OK thanks - i'm good.

[12:33] Samantha: Wrap up - to recap: action items, we'll send MSA/DPA + pricing + SOC2 links; Diego will coordinate the deep dive and perf tests; Ethan to return DPA redlines; Maria will confirm procurement PO process.

[12:52] Maria: Sounds good, thanks everyone.

[12:55] Samantha: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
